title: An Envelope
description:
Sangchul's office. As he set down the coffee, he slid a document envelope across the desk.

"Drop this off somewhere for me. An office in Yeoksam." A sticky note with the address was on it.

"It's easier for both of us if you don't ask what's inside." He smiled.

It was the first time. The first time this man had ever asked Minjun for anything. That the network hadn't been free — Minjun felt it now, in the weight of the envelope.

choices.text: Deliver it — decide not to ask
choices.result_text:
The envelope was light, but his hand was heavy.

Until he walked back out of that Yeoksam office, he never once asked what was inside. Not asking was an answer too.

choices.text: "I can't do this kind of thing." — hand it back
choices.result_text:
Sangchul took the envelope back. He didn't get angry.

"Sure. That's an answer too." That cool smile stayed with Minjun a long time.

title: Have You Looked in a Mirror?
description:
Fresh off her night shift, Daeun watched {name} for a long moment over her coffee cup. The fatigue of the night was still in the hands wrapped around the cup, and yet what she was looking at wasn't her own tiredness — it was {name}'s face.

"Minjun-ssi, have you looked in a mirror lately?" She asked it smiling, but her eyes weren't.

{name} glanced reflexively at the cafe window. A stranger's face was reflected there. For weeks he'd looked at nothing but his account balance. His face, it seemed, had noticed first.

Daeun didn't push for an answer. She just slowly stirred her cooling coffee.

description_if_moral.black:
Fresh off her night shift, Daeun watched Minjun for a long moment over her coffee cup. He noticed the receipt at the edge of the table before he noticed her gaze. Two coffees, 11,800 won.

The rest of today's spending added itself up in his head.

"Minjun-ssi, have you looked in a mirror lately?" Daeun asked with a smile. Her eyes weren't smiling.

Before answering, Minjun turned over the phone whose balance alert had just gone dark. He noticed Daeun's expression a moment too late.
description_if_moral.white:
Fresh off her night shift, Daeun still wore a beige cardigan over her uniform. One cuff had stretched slightly out of shape.

"Minjun-ssi, have you looked in a mirror lately?" she asked with a smile. Her eyes weren't smiling.

Minjun saw the worry in them before he heard the question. For weeks he'd looked at nothing but his account balance. Someone across the table had recognized his face before he had.

choices.text: Take the day off — go to the market together

text_if_moral.black: Clear half a day. Make up the lost time later and go to the market with her
text_if_moral.white: Take the day off. Go to the market with Daeun

choices.result_text:
That evening the two of them walked the market alleys. A bowl of sundae soup, three pairs of ten-thousand-won socks. For once he bought something that wasn't a number.

Steam rose off the fishcake broth, and Daeun held the paper cup in both hands, blowing on it.

Daeun laughed, and this time her eyes laughed too. {name} realized it was the first time all day he'd properly looked at them.

choices.text: "I'm fine." — turn back to work

text_if_moral.black: "I'm fine." Push the cup away and get back to work
text_if_moral.white: "I'm fine." Look away and get back to work

choices.result_text:
"Fine, sure." Daeun didn't press further. The sound of her cup meeting the table was a little louder than usual.

They both knew it was a lie. Knowing, and letting it pass — whether that was kindness or distance, {name} still had no answer by that night.

title: The Last Bus
description:
Eleven at night, Hyunsu called. He was at the terminal. Through the receiver came boarding announcements mixed with the sound of suitcase wheels.

"Heading down to my folks'. My father's memorial rite." Not much time before the bus, he said.

After a silence Hyunsu asked, "You're staying in Seoul, aren't you."

It sounded less like a question than a confirmation. Holidays, memorial rites — the one who stays in Seoul. Hyunsu's voice said he already knew that was {name}.

On the desk, the monitor still glowed with charts.

choices.text: See him off — go to the terminal
choices.result_text:
He closed the charts and caught a cab. Under the terminal lights Hyunsu grinned, startled. "What'd you come all the way here for."

As the bus backed out, Hyunsu raised a hand behind the window. {name} stood there until the taillights disappeared.

The way back, strangely, wasn't cold. Apparently the night wind had never been the problem.

choices.text: "I've got work." — say goodbye on the phone
choices.result_text:
"Oh, okay. Get home safe." He hung up and opened the charts again.

The numbers hadn't moved. Nothing had changed in those few minutes — and somehow that was what nagged at him.

Imagining the terminal lights and seeing them are different things. That night, he only imagined.

title: A Year Counted on One Hand
description:
Flipping the calendar, he stopped. He counted how many weeks in the past year he'd actually seen a person.

He folded his fingers down one at a time. The count ended before one hand was through. The remaining forty-some squares were all numbers. Buys, sells, interest due dates. Ballpoint pressed hard into every square.

The room was quiet. The kind of quiet where the hum of the refrigerator sounds unusually loud.

The account had grown. The calendar was honest. The two ledgers were telling different stories.

choices.text: This week, call someone
choices.result_text:
He dialed a number he hadn't used in a long time. Through three rings he considered hanging up. On the fourth, a glad voice answered.

They said nothing much. What are you even eating these days — that kind of talk. When he hung up, twenty minutes had passed.

In this week's square on the calendar, he wrote nothing. Some things stay without being written down.

choices.text: Close the ledger
choices.result_text:
He closed the calendar. Closing it was a kind of answer too.

Back at the desk, he checked the balance. The number was higher than yesterday's, and right now that felt more urgent.

The feeling of fingers folded partway down lingered faintly, into the night.

title: A Year Held Onto
description:
The same calendar, but he saw something different. Over the past year, he hadn't let go of anyone.

Between the numbers in each square, other entries were mixed in. Birthdays, a hospital visit, late dinners. Written in a different ink, scattered across the calendar — sparse, but steady.

He'd been slower than others for it. That was a fact. A calendar of nothing but numbers would have meant a thicker account.

Not a consolation but a confirmation. This is the time I spent. The hand turning the page wasn't heavy.

choices.text: Trust this pace
choices.result_text:
That slow isn't the same as losing — for the first time, he believed it.

He hung the calendar back on the wall, straightening it once where it tilted.

Outside the window was darkening, but his heart wasn't.

choices.text: "Is this why I'm behind?" — a flicker of worry
choices.result_text:
Closing the calendar, for a second, other people's accounts came to mind. The pace of those who had filled the same year with nothing but numbers.

Afraid the time spent holding on would come back as the price of being late. An honest fear.

Even lying in the dark with the light off, that arithmetic stayed on a while.

title: The Inner Room
description:
Sangchul led {name} to a room at the end of the hall.

The lighting was lower than in the usual office. The blinds were drawn all the way down, and the numbers on the papers on the table were of a different order of magnitude. Beside the ashtray, a few business cards lay face-down — names hidden.

"Figured you could sit in here now." Sangchul offered a seat. The voice was warm, as always.

It was a greyer room. The chair looked comfortable, which made it worse. It felt like something would begin the moment he sat down. The kind of beginning you can't walk back from.

description_if_known.sangchul_truth_known:
Sangchul led Minjun to a room at the end of the hall.

To eyes that knew the truth, even the lighting of that room looked different. The hand that had broken his father was now holding this door open.

"Figured you could sit in here now." The voice offering the seat was as warm as ever.

That was the coldest part.

choices.text: Go in
choices.result_text:
He sat down. The chair was softer than he'd expected.

The numbers grew, and by that much the room felt smaller. Sangchul didn't explain at length. In this room, apparently, explanations could be short.

Leaving, his shoulders were heavier than when he'd come in. The fluorescent light in the hallway stung his eyes.

choices.text: Turn back at the door
choices.result_text:
"Next time." He shut the door and stepped out into the hall.

Walking out under the fluorescent lights, no sound came from behind him. Sangchul was not a man who held people back. That was his way.

The strength it takes to turn away gets written in no ledger anywhere. Still, {name} figured it had earned its keep.

title: Hyunsu's Four Years
description:
Hyunsu got in touch. He'd failed the final interview. The end of four years.

And yet his voice was calm. Through the phone came the sound of him drinking something. Coffee, maybe. A man whose world has ended doesn't drink coffee.

"I'll just try again. This is the pace I live at."

{name}, searching for words of comfort, stopped instead. A man who had lost four years owned that sentence. {name}, in his third year in Seoul, did not.

choices.text: "I envy your pace." — say it honestly
choices.result_text:
He meant it. Hyunsu went quiet a moment, then laughed. "Look at you, saying things like that."

Behind the laugh came the sound of a cup being set down.

After hanging up, {name} doubted his own pace for the first time in a while. And for the first time, it occurred to him that doubt might not be an entirely bad thing.

choices.text: Just comfort him, swallow my own unease
choices.result_text:
"You'll be fine, you'll get it." He said the right thing, but his mouth tasted bitter.

He hung up and sat back down at the desk. For a moment the numbers on the monitor meant nothing at all.

That he envied Hyunsu's calm — he never managed to say it. {name} kept a separate drawer for the things he never managed to say.

title: Folded Time
description:
Washing his face, he looked up. The face in the mirror was unfamiliar.

The shadows under the eyes he knew; the look above them he didn't. While water dripped from his chin, {name} stood facing that face.

He'd run this far by folding time. Weekends that vanished for days at a stretch, calls put off, things stacked up still folded. The folded things hadn't disappeared — they had piled up somewhere. In this face, too.

One year left. How would he spend that year.

choices.text: Spend the last year differently
choices.result_text:
Drying his face with the towel, he decided. To unfold the folded things, one at a time.

Back in his room, the first thing he did was call one of the numbers he'd been putting off. While it rang, his heart beat a little fast.

Even if the account came a little later — so this face wouldn't turn unfamiliar again.

choices.text: Keep this pace — almost there
choices.result_text:
Almost there. {name} thought so and sat back down at the desk. The water marks on the mirror he left to dry.

Almost there — how far does that phrase actually reach? He folded the question and put it in the drawer.

His hands knew the folding motion well by now.

title: The Talk About After
description:
The word marriage was set into the air for the first time. No one quite sure who had raised it.

Once the word was out, the table went a little quiet. The noise of the cafe hadn't changed, but between the two of them the volume seemed to drop.

The plan sheet before the final sprint, and the weight of a person, sat on the same table for the first time. What can be written in numbers, and what can't.

{name} fidgeted with his cup. The cup had long gone cold, and handling a cold cup is the habit of a man postponing his answer.

description_if_known.daeun_romance_started:
Daeun cupped her glass in both hands.

"Minjun-ssi, I'm good at waiting. I just want to know what I'm waiting for." An unhurried voice. That's why it stayed longer.

The plan sheet before the final sprint, and the weight of this person, sat on the same table for the first time.
description_if_known.jiyeon_romance_started:
Jiyeon set her glass down.

"Oppa, let's talk. What comes after Gangnam?" Half-smiling, but her eyes were serious.

The plan sheet before the final sprint, and the weight of this person, sat on the same table for the first time.

choices.text: "Once this year ends." — make a concrete promise
choices.result_text:
Once said, it became a promise. He didn't set a date, but for the first time he spoke 'after' out loud.

The other person nodded quietly. Even after the nod stopped, the eyes stayed on {name}.

He pushed the cold cup aside and ordered a fresh one. It felt like an evening where that much, at least, was allowed.

choices.text: "Just a little more." — put it off
choices.result_text:
"Just a little more." {name} couldn't count how many times he'd said it.

The other person said they understood. Saying you understand doesn't always mean you do.

They left the cafe and walked in their separate directions. When he looked back after a few steps, the other was walking on without looking back.

title: A Business Card
description:
Clearing out a drawer, a single business card turned up. From the network days.

Thick stock. Paper heavy enough to feel between the fingertips. The ink was slightly smudged — sweat on his palm the day he received it, or just the years.

One card, and the rooms of that time came up with it. Low lighting, big numbers, the things he had agreed not to ask about.

What that time had left in his account — {name} did the tally, the card still in his hand. The tally didn't finish quickly.

description_if_known.sangchul_network_fully_cut:
Clearing out a drawer, a single business card turned up. The settling-up of one who had cut it off.

Slower, but every line in the account, Minjun could explain.

An account holding only money whose source he knew — thin, but light.
description_if_known.used_sangchul_knowingly:
Clearing out a drawer, a single business card turned up. The settling-up of one who had used it to the end.

Among the numbers stacked up fast, a few lines whose source he couldn't explain were mixed in.

Those few lines didn't erase.

choices.text: Throw the card away
choices.result_text:
He dropped it in the bin. The smudged name vanished between the papers.

He finished clearing the drawer. His hands were lighter than before.

With that, one thing got put in order. The kind of ordering no ledger records.

choices.text: Slip it back into the wallet
choices.result_text:
He tucked the card back into the inner fold of his wallet. The thick stock stood out slightly among the other cards.

The thought that he might use it someday hadn't quite disappeared yet.

The snap of the wallet closing sounded louder than usual.
